- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+), model tends to overshoot and then sharply correct — overreacting to short-term volatility.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the 30-day forecast, suggesting it underestimates downward trends or fails to capture mean reversion.
- Forecast often lags true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends — model reacts too slowly to falling prices.
- Model exhibits high variance in early days but stabilizes toward end — may be overfitting to recent noise or underestimating volatility decay.
- When true price drops below 75, model often fails to recognize the trend and continues forecasting higher — underestimates downside risk.
- Model tends to overcorrect after minor upward moves, creating artificial “reversals” that don’t align with actual market behavior.
- In cases of prolonged downward trend, model fails to show sufficient mean reversion — continues to predict decline even after price stabilizes.
